title: EnFractal room manifest (room.json)
description: The immutable baseline of one room: shell, object instances, spawns and light hints. Written by the capture exporter (or by hand for test rooms), read by the game. Its identity pin is the SHA-256 of the file bytes; every other file in the room directory is pinned through the files list, and each asset.json pins its own files. Runtime changes never rewrite this file; they live in room state. Every string in it is untrusted data. Captured rooms are written to the player's user data (user://rooms/<room_id>/), never into the repository.

axes.description: Godot convention: +Y up, -Z forward, right-handed, 1 unit = 1 metre.

bounds.description: Playable volume. Avatars and creations outside it are recovered; effects are clipped to it.

site.description: Where the room stands, as far as the sun is concerned, and no more. The look works out the sun's height and direction from it; a room without one gets the look's fallback site. Deliberately coarse: whole degrees of latitude and a quarter hour of solar noon say which sun a room gets and nothing about where it is. There is no longitude, no place name and no finer latitude, and the schema refuses them, so a manifest that is shared or exported cannot carry a location (AGENTS.md: strip location metadata from anything written). Review M5 of the Look lane: these three numbers used to live in the shared style preset.

latitude_deg.description: Whole degrees north of the equator (south is negative), within 66 degrees of it.

neg_z_bearing_deg.description: The compass bearing of the room's -Z axis in whole degrees, clockwise from north: 0 means -Z points north (so -X is west), 90 means it points east.

solar_noon_h.description: The clock hour (local standard time, daylight saving removed) when the sun is highest on average, on a quarter hour. 12 is a room at the middle of its time zone; this is the only trace of longitude and is coarser than a time zone's width.

default_style.description: Style the room opens with. The active style is pinned in room state, so restyling never rewrites the manifest.

files.description: Every file the manifest references (shell meshes, asset.json files, reference media), with hashes. Files not listed here must not be loaded.

extensions.description: Experiments (common.schema.json), and the keys the mechanics round types: x_fractals, the Fractals the island places, and x_island_tutorial (M0, 14 October 2026), x_summit, the island's summit (the second contract round, 15 October), and x_firepits, the island's firepits (decision 74, 24 October). The landscape exporter writes them from the generator's package (M4); readers that do not know them ignore them, as every extension.

x_island_tutorial.description: True for an island the opening menu lists first as a tutorial (none is locked). Absent: false.

privacy.description: Rooms are people's homes and businesses. Sharing later depends on these being true statements.

points_m.description: Coplanar, simple polygon. Winding is counter-clockwise seen from inside the room, so the right-hand normal points into the room; thickness extrudes away from the room.

drawn.description: Optional, default true. False makes a colliding part collision-only: it is never rendered (a climbing pole hidden inside a tree's leaves, a one-sided cap to stand on). Mesh collision is one-sided: a body passes through a face from behind. A part that is neither drawn nor collides is invalid.

size_m.description: Width along the host surface, then height.

leads_to.description: Another room of the same house. Unused until rooms connect.

asset.description: objects/<asset_id>/asset.json. Several instances may share one asset.

transform.description: Placement of the asset's pivot (bottom centre of its bounds) in room coordinates.

initial_parts.description: Initial articulation per asset part, 0 closed to 1 fully open.

light_hint.description: A light the capture saw. The style preset decides how strongly to honour it.

reference.description: Review material for agents and the founder. Excluded from game builds.

plant_copies.description: Plants, trees and stones drawn as copies of one mesh per set: the 10x world (13 October 2026), promoted from the scale experiment's x_landscape_instances. Each set lists its copies in one table file of fixed-width little-endian rows (the layout is in contracts/README.md, 'Plant copies'), sorted by 8 m tile and then by x and z, behind a tile index. A copy is the entity plant:<set>-<row> (common.schema.json plant_id). Copies are part of the immutable baseline: what fire, seeding and replanting do to them lives in room state, never here. No manifest object rests on a copy, and copies count toward no other cap (objects, shell parts).

tile_m.description: The side of a table tile in metres: a copy at (x, z) is in tile (floor(x / 8), floor(z / 8)). Fire's ground-fuel grid and far fires use the same tiles.

groups.description: How many groves and patches the room has: copies the generator placed together (a grove of trees, a patch of flowers, a bed of reeds), numbered 1 to groups across every set, each number used by at least one copy. A copy in no group has group 0. This lets perception say 'a grove of 40' instead of listing each tree.

plant_set.description: One kind of copy: one mesh (with lighter meshes for distance), one table of rows. Trees carry their climbing collision in their rows (kind tree); the drawn mesh itself never collides.

set.description: The set's name, unique in the room, and the first half of its copies' ids (plant:<set>-<row>). No hyphen, so the row after the last '-' is unambiguous.

prototype.description: The landscape prototype the copies are drawn from (a kit name such as broadleaf, or a generator prototype such as daisies). Provenance only.

kind.description: plant (grass, flowers, ferns, heather, reeds, shrubs), tree (climbable: its rows carry the climbing collision) or stone.

species.description: What grows (or lies) there, for perception, fire, seeds and replanting: a lowercase name such as grass, daisies, heather, broadleaf, conifer or rock. Several sets may share one. Untrusted like every name.

collides.description: none: drawn only, bodies pass through. tree_climb: the row's trunk, pole and caps collide (trees only; README 'Plant copies'). solid: each copy collides with the convex hull of its level-0 mesh under the row's transform (stones).

fuel_class.description: How a copy burns, for the fire rebuild: none (never burns: stones), grass (fine and fast: grass, reeds), herb (leafy: flowers, ferns, heather), shrub (woody brush), broadleaf or conifer (trees). Fire's numbers per class belong to the host and the island rules, never to the room.

seeds.description: Whether its copies set seed: seeds of its species can be gathered from them, and a copy lost to fire is replanted and regrows. Stones never seed.

mesh.description: The copy at full detail: a self-contained GLB in the prototype's own frame, metres, pivot at the bottom centre (its lowest point at y 0, centred in x and z), unscaled. Its materials name their landscape roles as the shell's landscape meshes do.

triangle_count.description: Triangles in mesh, as its GLB holds them.

lods.description: Lighter meshes for distance, in order, each lighter than the one before and in the same frame. The game chooses by distance; the data names no ranges.

table.description: The set's rows: one table file (README, 'Plant copies'), listed in files with its hash and size like every other file.

cap_slots.description: Trees only: cap slots in each row (a broadleaf has up to 5 crowns, a conifer 1). A row uses cap_count of them; the rest are zero bytes.

tiles.description: Entries in the table's tile index: the 8 m tiles that hold at least one copy.

count.description: Rows in the table: the set's copies, plant:<set>-0 to plant:<set>-<count - 1>.

terrain_tiles.description: The land cut into 16 m tiles with distance detail (the 10x world). Each listed part's GLB holds one node per tile and level, named tile_<tx>_<tz>_lod<level>: tx = floor(x / 16) and tz = floor(z / 16) in decimal ('-' before a negative, no leading zeros), level the index into levels. Every node in such a GLB is a tile node: a root of its scene with a mesh, no transform and no children, its positions in room metres inside its tile's square. Every tile of a part has every level. Level 0 is the finest and the walkable ground: a colliding part collides through level 0 only, and the game draws one level per tile, choosing by distance. Shell part ids, support targets and the 128-part cap are unchanged: a tiled part is still one shell part.

tile_m.description: The side of a terrain tile in metres.

levels.description: The levels of detail, finest first, each coarser than the one before: today 0.1 m (with finer detail where a body meets the land), 0.4 m and 1.6 m.

grid_m.description: The level's nominal grid spacing in metres.

parts.description: The tiled shell parts, each a mesh part listed once. Parts not listed (water, scenery, collision-only aids) keep one mesh drawn whole.

tiles.description: How many tiles the part's GLB holds (each at every level).

x_fractals.description: The Fractals the island places (docs/game/MECHANICS.md section 6): real small things at the island's scale, at crests the body can reach by climb, from the island's budget (the rules pack's fractals block, which also says how they are spent). Part of the pinned baseline: a Fractal picked up is room state (the island save), never an edit here, so adding them changes the room's fingerprint and the fixture rebuilds itself.

typed.description: Whether each Fractal carries its kind (the rules pack's typed flag, off by default: untyped).

x_fractal.description: One Fractal: its id (the entity the player's item.pickup names) and where it rests, its pivot at its bottom centre in room metres.

kind.description: Typed Fractals only: a heart or the next stamina band.

reach_band.description: Optional: the lowest stamina band (1, the starting bar) from which the generator's walk reaches it, for the reach report; absent when not measured.

x_firepits.description: The island's firepits (docs/game/MECHANICS.md decisions 62 and 74): spread evenly over the island by the generator, one per 250 m2 of standable dry land, at least 4 m apart, 1 m from any Fractal and 3 m from the starting campfire (which is the kernel's own, in front of the player's spawn, and never listed here). The kernel numbers them in this order (firepit:1 first: the generator lists the nearest the start first) and checks each spot on the island's own ground; one that does not check is left out and the kernel's own spread fills its place. Part of the pinned baseline, like x_fractals: a firepit lit is room state (the island save), never an edit here. Absent: the kernel spreads the firepits itself.

x_firepit.description: One firepit: where it stands, its pivot at its bottom centre on its ground, in room metres.

x_summit.description: The island's summit (docs/game/MECHANICS.md section 6): the top of the one landmark whose route corridor the generator cuts (M4). Reaching it with the Gubble sets the "past the tutorial" achievement, opens the second knack slot, earns a souvenir and unlocks the overview camera; the player has reached it with their feet within radius_m of center_m. Part of the pinned baseline, like x_fractals: the exporter writes it from the generator's package. Absent: the island has no summit yet.

center_m.description: The summit's top, on its ground, in room metres.

radius_m.description: How far from center_m still counts as on the summit.

landmark.description: Optional: the generator's id for the landmark the summit tops; never shown as instructions.

top_band.description: Optional: the band the corridor's highest ledge needs. The founder, 15 October: bands 7 to 8 on the garage, so its summit waits for a return visit, Bubble lift or a built ladder.
